transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

To be honest, it's a bit hard for me to admit, but lately I feel like how I see myself depends almost completely on what I weigh or how my body looks. My wife noticed how much this was weighing on me and encouraged me to see my doctor, who then referred me here.

To help me understand your eating habits better, do you find yourself strictly limiting how much food you eat, or do you experience times where you feel you lose control and eat a large amount of food?

I actually experience both of those things as part of a cycle. Late at night, it feels like a switch flips and I lose control, standing at the counter eating huge amounts of leftovers and cereal until I'm uncomfortably full. Then the next day, I'll try to "reset" by strictly limiting myself to just coffee and maybe an apple until dinner.
To help me understand your physical health, could you share your current height and weight, and let me know if you've recently lost a significant amount of weight?

I don't have my exact height and weight on hand right now, to be honest. I haven't had any massive weight loss, just these small, stressful fluctuations of a couple of pounds that make me feel completely out of control.
Besides restricting your food the next day, do you ever make yourself throw up, use laxatives, or exercise excessively to try to prevent weight gain after these eating episodes?

It's really hard to admit, but yes, I do. On the worst nights, I'll go into the bathroom and run the shower so my family won't hear me making myself throw up. Other times, I force myself to go on long, punishing walks after my closing shifts even when I'm completely exhausted, just to try to make up for what I ate.
How often do these episodes of losing control and then throwing up or exercising excessively occur, and for how many months has this been happening?

It's become almost a routine now where these episodes happen about once or twice a week. This whole pattern has been going on for about six months, starting shortly after our second child was born and things got really chaotic at home.
Do you have a specific target weight that you feel you absolutely must stay below, and is this weight much lower than what a doctor would consider healthy for your height?

I don't really have a specific target weight in mind, and I'm not sure if what I want is considered medically unhealthy. It's more that I just completely panic whenever I see the scale go up even a pound or two.
Do you experience an intense, overwhelming fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even if your weight is currently in a normal or healthy range?

Yes, absolutely. If the scale is even two pounds higher in the morning, I spend the whole day panicking that I'm on a slippery slope to getting fat like my dad did in his forties. That fear immediately makes me start mentally cutting out more and more foods that I decide I'm not allowed to have anymore.

Because all criteria are fully met, F50.3 (Atypical bulimia nervosa) is ruled out, leaving F50.2 as the final diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the diagnostic criteria for Bulimia Nervosa (ICD-10: F50.2). They describe recurrent episodes of binge eating characterized by a loss of control, occurring 1-2 times per week for approximately six months. To counteract weight gain, the patient engages in inappropriate compensatory behaviors, including self-induced vomiting, excessive exercise, and severe dietary restriction. Their self-evaluation is unduly influenced by body shape and weight, and they experience an intense fear of gaining weight.
